title: Separate anatomical rig segmentation from dense Body sampling
description:
## Explicit anatomy requirement

The rigging system must be Spore-like in its generality: it must NOT be modeled as a biped-vs-quadruped system. Any authored creature may have any number of limbs, in any authored order, of any supported limb part type, attached at any valid position along the Body. Limb count, ordering, and placement are data; they must never select a hard-coded locomotion/anatomy mode.

## Summary
Introduce a compact anatomical rig layer so dense Body morphology samples no longer define long-term character-rig topology. Compact must not mean a four-bone caricature: the anatomical layer retains multiple articulated Body segments along the canonical headward and tailward arcs while remaining independent of morphology sampling density.

## Current implementation
`AnatomicalBodyRigLayout` derives a single pelvis root plus multiple density-independent headward and tailward Body segments and an explicit head terminal. Segment boundaries are chosen in canonical normalized arc-length space, not by raw sample index, so denser morphology sampling does not silently remove or add character joints. Direct Body-rooted limb attachment evidence is treated uniformly regardless of limb count or part type. Body-rooted attachments resolve to the compact backbone segment containing their Body-space position, allowing arbitrary attachment locations instead of biped/quadruped landmark modes. Dense Body samples remain the morphology/SDF representation.

## Acceptance
- Compact topology is stable across Body sampling density.
- The implementation contains no biped/quadruped topology branch or limb-count mode.
- Compact Body topology retains multiple articulated segments on sufficiently long headward and tailward regions; it must not collapse an entire curved chest-to-head region into one bone.
- Any number of direct Body-rooted limb chains can coexist and remain independently addressable.
- Supported authored limb part types can coexist without type-specific topology modes.
- Authored limb order does not affect semantic bone identity or parent selection.
- Valid limb attachments at arbitrary Body positions resolve deterministically to the containing anatomical backbone segment.
- Valid generated skeletons retain a single semantic root.
- Limb/mirror attachment behavior remains deterministic.
- Weight preparation consumes compact Body metadata rather than legacy body_j sample IDs.
- Representative multi-limb runtime validation is still required before closure.

## Design limits
Do not add a cosmetic synthetic locomotion root. The current world-space identity-host pose contract remains in force until a deliberate local/root-relative pose-space design is introduced. Foot grounding remains separate.

## Status
InProgress: compact segmented Body topology implemented; final Unity/generated-creature validation remains open.

## Evidence
`SkeletonInferrerTests.Infer_ArbitraryLimbCountPlacementOrderAndTypeDoesNotSelectSpeciesMode` exercises five chains using mixed supported limb types, deliberately scrambled authored order, and distinct Body attachment positions. `AnatomicalBodyRigLayoutTests` now also asserts multiple headward/tailward segments, curved-centerline direction changes, density-independent topology, and arbitrary attachment mapping. Additional anatomy and binding tests cover density independence, mirror behavior, and compact Body radius sharing.

See the skeleton/animation audit documents under `docs/audits/` on branch `audit/skeleton-animation-improvements-2026-09-07`.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: New explicit requirement from user: like Spore, the system must support any number of limbs in any order at any valid position on the body; it must not collapse into biped-vs-quadruped-specific rigging modes. Generalized `AnatomicalBodyRigLayout` accordingly: all direct Body-rooted limb attachments contribute uniformly, pelvis derivation uses robust median attachment evidence without part-type checks, and attachment selection uses the containing compact backbone segment. Added multi-limb arbitrary-order/position regression coverage.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Expanded the executable invariant: the arbitrary-limb regression now mixes supported `Arm`, `Leg`, and generic `Limb` part types while preserving five independent chains, scrambled authoring order, and distinct Body attachment positions. No runtime topology mode is selected by count, ordering, or type.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: User-visible regression: the compact Body rig rendered most of the Body as a single chest-to-nose bone on `dinus_uprightus`. Corrected `AnatomicalBodyRigLayout` so compact topology remains density-independent but retains multiple canonical-arc Body articulation segments on both the headward and tailward branches. Updated runtime regressions to prove multi-segment topology and curved-centerline direction changes, and updated `RigDebugView` to draw each semantic segment from its explicit Position to EndPosition. Unity/generated-creature validation remains required before closure.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Audit synthesis 2026-09-07: the supplied live-use audit's claim that `AnatomicalBodyRigLayout` always emits four Body bones is stale/refuted at the current fixed point `dd9f946`. Source now emits a pelvis anchor, indexed spine and tail segments using `BodySegmentArcStep`, and a head terminal. `AnatomicalBodyRigLayoutTests` prove multiple branches, curved direction changes, and density-independent topology. Do not create a follow-on segmentation task or merge this mechanism into TSK-0152. Retain TSK-0148 as the canonical owner because Unity/generated-creature deformation validation remains open. Provenance: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-rig-liveuse-audit-2026-09-07.md`, Finding 1.
